Casting an object to a boolean in PHP always results in true.

The magic constant __NAMESPACE__ indeed returns the fully qualified name of the current namespace, or an empty string if the file is in the global namespace.

PHP allows use statements inside functions, and the import applies only to the function's local scope.
By default, PHP arrays are value types and are copied when assigned to another variable, meaning modifications to one do not affect the other unless reference syntax is used.
In PHP, arrays are value types, so $b is a copy of $a; modifying $b does not affect $a.

PHP copies the array for by-value foreach, so external mutations during the loop are not visible.
Static properties are shared among all instances of a class, so changes in one object are visible in others.
In PHP, array keys of type boolean are cast to integers (true becomes 1, false becomes 0) rather than remaining as boolean keys.

A generator in PHP is a one-time iterator; once it is fully consumed (reaches the end of its loop), it cannot be rewound and traversed again using rewind(). You would need to recreate the generator.

In PHP, the password_hash() function automatically generates and includes a random salt, so there is no need to provide a salt separately.

The $_SESSION superglobal is only populated with session data after the session_start() function has been called and the session has been initiated.

In Clean and Onion architectures, the Dependency Rule dictates that source code dependencies must point only inward, toward the core business logic, ensuring inner layers remain independent of outer details like frameworks or databases.
Domain entities should be framework-agnostic and typically extend only base PHP classes or use standard libraries, without directly importing Doctrine or Symfony dependencies.
Controllers and views belong to the presentation layer, not the business-logic layer.
In Onion Architecture, the innermost layer consists of the core business entities and domain logic that are independent of any external framework or technology.
Tools like deptrac analyze static dependencies and can enforce layer boundaries by failing the build when forbidden calls are detected.
A use case (interactor) should not accept framework-specific types like HTTP requests or EntityManagers, as this violates decoupling and makes the use case harder to test and reuse.
In Domain-Driven Design, a Repository abstracts the storage mechanism and provides a collection-like interface for managing entities.

In clean architecture, the domain and use cases depend on abstractions (interfaces), so changing the database (e.g., from PostgreSQL to another) only affects the adapters/frameworks layer, leaving the core domain and use cases unchanged.
An aggregate in Domain-Driven Design is a cluster of related entities and value objects that are treated as a single unit for consistency purposes, not simply a database table.
Value Objects are defined by their data rather than their identity, and changing their state typically involves creating a new instance to maintain immutability.
In Domain-Driven Design, the aggregate root is the single external entry point and guarantees consistency within the aggregate.
In Domain-Driven Design, repositories are defined for aggregate roots to ensure that the entire aggregate is treated as a single unit of consistency and transactional integrity.

Ubiquitous Language is a core concept in Domain-Driven Design (DDD) where the terminology used in the codebase matches the business language used by domain experts and developers to minimize miscommunication.

In the context of set theory and model theory, the 'universe' or 'domain' defines the collection of objects within which the axioms and language of a model are consistent and interpreted; outside this set, symbols may refer to different objects in other models.
DDD recommends rich domain models with behavior encapsulated in domain objects, whereas anemic models push logic into services.
In Domain-Driven Design, Bounded Contexts define clear boundaries where specific models apply, allowing the same term to have different meanings and implementations in different contexts.
Services in the Symfony dependency injection container are instantiated lazily, meaning they are only created when they are first requested (e.g., via injection or get()).
The Symfony console command to list all registered routes is 'debug:router'.
Symfony's autowiring feature automatically resolves and injects dependencies, so services do not need to be manually declared in services.yaml unless necessary for configuration or binding.
Twig compiles templates into optimized PHP classes and caches them (typically in the app's cache directory) to avoid re-compilation on every request.
In the dev environment, Symfony uses the debug container which caches compiled services and only rebuilds them when tracked configuration or class files change, rather than on every single request.
The APP_ENV environment variable is used to define the current Symfony environment.
Symfony's routing system uses reflection to invoke controller methods, and private methods cannot be accessed from outside the class scope by the router.
Event subscribers and listeners are both registered with the dispatcher and executed in the order defined by their priority and registration order, not based on their role (subscriber vs. listener).
The legacy Guard authentication system was indeed removed in Symfony 6.0, and modern authentication is now built upon the new Authenticator system.

In Symfony 7.x, Doctrine annotations are still supported and not yet fully removed, though they are deprecated.

Symfony always performs server-side validation to ensure data integrity, regardless of client-side HTML5 checks.
The Symfony MakerBundle command to generate a form class is make:form.
Symfony stores the user's password in the session as a hashed value (typically via the password hasher service) rather than in plain text, for security.
Symfony 4+ adopts a modular configuration approach where bundle-specific settings are stored in individual files under the config/packages/ directory.
It is a common best practice to commit a .env file with development defaults (containing non-sensitive values) while keeping actual secrets in an untracked .env.local or similar file.
The debug:container command in Symfony is used to list all registered services and their aliases.

While generally discouraged for core logic due to performance and immutability, the Symfony container does provide the setParameter() method which can technically be called at runtime to modify parameters before they are used.
Since Symfony 3.4 (and 4.0), services are private by default (public: false) to allow for better optimization and removal of unused services.
A bundle can function without a configuration file if it does not require custom settings, or if it is used purely for extending Symfony via a service provider.
In Symfony, the standard syntax for injecting environment variables into configuration files like services.yaml is %env(VAR_NAME)%.
In Symfony, the APP_DEBUG environment variable controls the debug mode, which enables the profiler and other debugging features.
By default, a single message is dispatched to and handled by exactly one handler, although middleware can allow for multiple handlers to process the same message sequentially.
The sync transport processes the message immediately in the same process, whereas async transports queue it for later processing by a worker.
The command to start the Messenger queue worker in Symfony is messenger:consume.
Retry configuration, including the retry strategy, is defined on the transport, as part of the transport definition in config/packages/messenger.yaml.
By default, Symfony Messenger uses PhpSerializer to serialize messages, not JSONSerializer.

Symfony follows a release schedule with major versions every two years and minor versions every six months, typically in May and November.

Symfony provides a dedicated UPGRADE guide in the CHANGELOG or documentation for every major release to detail backward-incompatible changes and migration steps.

Twig's {{ }} syntax is for outputting expressions or variables, not for executing arbitrary PHP code directly.
Twig enables auto-escaping by default for variables printed with the `{{ }}` syntax to prevent XSS attacks.
The |e (escape) filter in Twig escapes a string to make it safe for output in an HTML context by default.
The number_format filter in twig/intl-extra formats a number according to a given locale.

Twig allows variable declaration and modification within templates using the set tag.
The dump() function in Twig outputs the debug information of a variable using the Symfony VarDumper component.
Bootstrap is primarily a front-end framework offering CSS and JavaScript components, rather than a JavaScript framework for building Single Page Applications (SPAs) like React, Angular, or Vue.
The 'container' class in Bootstrap provides a responsive wrapper that has a fixed maximum width that changes at each media query breakpoint.

In Bootstrap and many CSS frameworks, utility classes with numerical suffixes (like .mt-3) map to the spacing scale defined by CSS variables, where the value is typically a multiple of the base spacing unit ($spacer or --bs-spacer).
The data-bs-toggle attribute is used in Bootstrap 5 to trigger interactive components like dropdowns or modals.
Bootstrap 5 removed the jQuery dependency and uses vanilla JavaScript for its components.

Doctrine ORM does not automatically create tables at runtime; it requires explicit schema management, such as running migrations or using tools like `orm:schema-tool:update`.
EntityManager::persist() marks an entity as managed and schedules the INSERT statement for the next flush() call.

DQL (Doctrine Query Language) is object-oriented and uses entities and fields, unlike SQL which uses tables and columns.
In Doctrine ORM, the find() method returns null if no entity with the specified primary key is found.
By default, DoctrineBundle (via Doctrine) does not automatically call flush() at the end of every request; you must explicitly call it or configure a listener to do so.
For managed entities, the Unit of Work automatically detects changes to their properties and persists them upon flush(), making an explicit persist() call unnecessary for modifications.
In Doctrine ORM, the remove() method marks an entity for deletion, but the actual SQL DELETE query is only executed when the EntityManager is flushed.
In PostgreSQL's MVCC, readers do not block writers and writers do not block readers; they operate concurrently by reading snapshots or creating new versions of rows.
The EXPLAIN statement in SQL is used to retrieve the execution plan of a query without actually running it.

string_agg(column, separator) is the PostgreSQL aggregate function that concatenates strings with a specified separator.
Plain VACUUM only marks space as reusable within the table file; it does not shrink the file or return space to the OS. Only VACUUM FULL (or similar) does this.
The PARTITION BY clause in a window function definition divides the result set into partitions or groups over which the function is computed.
READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads but does not protect against non-repeatable reads, which requires REPEATABLE READ or higher.
In PostgreSQL, if no explicit transaction block (BEGIN/COMMIT) is specified, each SQL statement is automatically committed upon successful completion.
COMMIT is the SQL command used to save all changes made during the current transaction.
Indexes are used to quickly locate rows for UPDATE and DELETE operations when the WHERE clause matches an indexed column, significantly improving performance.
SAVEPOINT allows rolling back a transaction to a specific point without aborting the entire transaction.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query to collect actual runtime statistics, whereas plain EXPLAIN only shows the plan without execution.
pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension that adds vector types and indexes for embedding search.

Partial indexes are a feature of PostgreSQL, not PHP (a language, not a database), and in PHP you would use a database-agnostic layer to interact with the database, but the statement describes a database feature, not a PHP one.

PostgreSQL's SERIALIZABLE isolation level is implemented using predicate locking (or serializable snapshot isolation), which tracks conflicts between transactions, rather than simply locking the rows that are read (which is characteristic of REPEATABLE READ or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE).
HTTP status code 201 (Created) indicates that the request has been fulfilled and a new resource has been created as a result.
HTTP status code 204 No Content indicates a successful request where the server did not return a body.
HTTP defines idempotent methods as those where repeated invocations have the same effect as a single invocation, and DELETE is explicitly listed as idempotent in RFC 9110.
The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is sent by the server, not the client, to indicate which origin is permitted to access the response.
HTTP status code 429 is specifically defined for rate limiting, informing the client that they have sent too many requests in a given amount of time.
HTTP status codes 4xx indicate client errors, while 5xx codes indicate server errors.
The Content-Type header field is used to specify the media type (MIME type) of the resource.
RFC 5789 states that PATCH is intended to represent a set of modifications to be applied to a resource, and unlike PUT, it is not required to be idempotent.
Using == is susceptible to timing attacks; hash_equals() or === should be used for constant-time comparison.
CSRF tokens are session-bound and verified server-side to ensure the request originates from the legitimate user session.
The HTTP header 'Content-Security-Policy' is used to define a whitelist of valid sources for browser resources.

OAuth 2.0 is an authorization framework, not an authentication protocol; it delegates authorization to access resources on behalf of a user, whereas OpenID Connect or SAML are used for authentication to determine identity.
Validating input before storage is good practice, but the primary defense against XSS is encoding/escaping output when rendering it in the browser, not just validating it on the server.

In the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow, the authorization server redirects the user's agent back to the client's redirect_uri with an authorization code, which the client then exchanges for an access token.
Refresh tokens are designed with a longer expiration than access tokens specifically to allow clients to request new access tokens without requiring the user to re-authenticate.
A password salt is intended to be stored publicly alongside the hash; it only needs to be unique, not secret.
PHPUnit requires test classes to extend PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase in order to access its test runner functionality and assertions.
In PHPUnit, setUp() runs before each test method, while setUpBeforeClass() runs once before all tests.
A data provider in PHP unit testing frameworks like PHPUnit can return multiple sets of arguments, allowing a test to run multiple times with different data.
The expectException() method is used to declare an expectation that an exception of the specified class will be thrown.
In PHPUnit, a mock object is used to verify interactions (like method calls), while a stub is used to return pre-defined data.
PHPUnit 10 introduced PHP attributes as the primary and recommended method for defining metadata like data providers, deprecating the docblock annotation style.
PHPUnit supports test dependencies using the depends() annotation/method, allowing one test to depend on the result or data of another.
The --random-order option in PHPUnit allows test suites or methods to be executed in a random sequence.
